# Problem 1: OOP Programming

## a. For the waldCI class, define some followings

```{r}
# 1. Define the S4 class and its validity rules
setClass("waldCI",
         slots = c(level = "numeric",mean = "numeric",
                   sterr = "numeric"))

.is_scalar_number <- function(x) {
  is.numeric(x) && length(x) == 1L && is.finite(x)
}
setValidity("waldCI", function(object) {
  if (!.is_scalar_number(object@level) ||
      object@level <= 0 || object@level >= 1) {
    return("level must be between 0 and 1")
  }
  if (!.is_scalar_number(object@mean)) {
    return("mean must be a finite number")
  }
  if (!.is_scalar_number(object@sterr) ||
      object@sterr <= 0) {
    return("sterr must be positive and finite")
  }
  TRUE
})
```

```{r}
# 2. Validator
.critical_z <- function(level) {
  qnorm((1 - level) / 2, lower.tail = FALSE)
}

makeCI <- function(level, mean = NULL, sterr = NULL,
                   lb = NULL, ub = NULL) {
  if (!.is_scalar_number(level) ||
      level <= 0 || level >= 1) {stop("Invalid confidence level")
  }

  by_estimate <- !is.null(mean) && !is.null(sterr) &&
    is.null(lb) && is.null(ub)

  by_limits <- !is.null(lb) && !is.null(ub) &&
    is.null(mean) && is.null(sterr)

  if (!by_estimate && !by_limits) {
    stop("Provide mean/sterr or lb/ub, but not both")
  }

  if (by_limits) {
    if (!.is_scalar_number(lb) ||
        !.is_scalar_number(ub) || lb >= ub) {
      stop("Invalid confidence interval bounds")
    }
    mean <- lb + (ub - lb) / 2
    sterr <- (ub - lb) / (2 * .critical_z(level))
  }
  result <- new("waldCI", level = level,
                mean = mean, sterr = sterr)
  validObject(result)
  result
}
```

```{r}
# 3. A show method
.ci_bounds <- function(object) {
  margin <- .critical_z(object@level) * object@sterr
  c(lb = object@mean - margin,ub = object@mean + margin)
}

setMethod("show", "waldCI", function(object) {
  b <- .ci_bounds(object)
  cat(sprintf("%.1f%% Wald CI: [%.5f, %.5f]\n",
              100 * object@level, b[1], b[2]))

  invisible(object)
})
```

```{r}
# 4. Accessors
setGeneric("level",
           function(object) standardGeneric("level"))
setMethod("level", "waldCI",
          function(object) object@level)
setMethod("mean", "waldCI",
          function(x, ...) x@mean)
setGeneric("sterr",
           function(object) standardGeneric("sterr"))
setMethod("sterr", "waldCI",
          function(object) object@sterr)
setGeneric("lb",
           function(object) standardGeneric("lb"))
setMethod("lb", "waldCI",
          function(object) unname(.ci_bounds(object)[1]))
setGeneric("ub",
           function(object) standardGeneric("ub"))
setMethod("ub", "waldCI",
          function(object) unname(.ci_bounds(object)[2]))
```

```{r}
# 5. Setters
setGeneric("level<-",
           function(object, value) standardGeneric("level<-"))
setReplaceMethod("level", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
  object@level <- value
  validObject(object)
  object
})

setGeneric("mean<-",
           function(object, value) standardGeneric("mean<-"))
setReplaceMethod("mean", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
  object@mean <- value
  validObject(object)
  object
})

setGeneric("sterr<-",
           function(object, value) standardGeneric("sterr<-"))
setReplaceMethod("sterr", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
  object@sterr <- value
  validObject(object)
  object
})

setGeneric("lb<-",
           function(object, value) standardGeneric("lb<-"))
setReplaceMethod("lb", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
  makeCI(level = object@level,
         lb = value, ub = ub(object))
})

setGeneric("ub<-",
           function(object, value) standardGeneric("ub<-"))
setReplaceMethod("ub", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
  makeCI(level = object@level,
         lb = lb(object), ub = value)
})
```

```{r}
# 6. Contains method
setGeneric("contains",
           function(object, value) standardGeneric("contains"))
setMethod("contains", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
  if (!.is_scalar_number(value)) {
    stop("value must be one finite number")
  }
  value >= lb(object) && value <= ub(object)
})
```

```{r}
# 7. Overlap method
setGeneric("overlap",
           function(x, y) standardGeneric("overlap"))
setMethod("overlap",
          signature(x = "waldCI", y = "waldCI"),
          function(x, y) {
            max(lb(x), lb(y)) <= min(ub(x), ub(y))
          })
```

```{r}
# 8. Numeric conversion
setGeneric("as.numeric")
setMethod("as.numeric", "waldCI", function(x, ...) {
  unname(.ci_bounds(x))
})
```

```{r}
# 9. Transform confidence interval
transformCI <- function(ci, fn) {
  if (!is(ci, "waldCI")) {
    stop("ci must be a waldCI object")
  }
  if (!is.function(fn)) {
    stop("fn must be a function")
  }
  warning("Only monotonic transformations are valid.",
          call. = FALSE)
  new_bounds <- vapply(as.numeric(ci), fn, numeric(1))
  if (!all(is.finite(new_bounds))) {
    stop("Transformed bounds must be finite")
  }
  new_bounds <- sort(new_bounds)
  makeCI(level = level(ci),
         lb = new_bounds[1],
         ub = new_bounds[2])
}
```

# Problem 2: data-table

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(nzelect)
library(data.table)
ten <- fread("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azhou5849/tennis-atp-sackmann-data/master/atp_matches_2019.csv")
stopifnot(is.data.table(ten))
```

## a. How many tournaments took place in 2019?

```{r}
events <- unique(ten[, .(tourney_name, tourney_level)])
events[, event_label := fifelse(tourney_level == "D",
                              "Davis Cup", tourney_name)]
count_a <- events[, .(tournaments = uniqueN(event_label))]
print(count_a)
```

So there are only 69 unique tournaments.

## b. Did any player win more than one tournament? If so, how many players won more than one tournament, and how many tournaments did the most winning player(s) win?

```{r}
finals <- unique(
  ten[round == "F" & tourney_level != "D",
      .(tourney_id, winner_id, winner_name)],
  by = "tourney_id"
)

title_counts <- finals[, .(titles = .N),
                       by = .(winner_id, winner_name)][
                         order(-titles, winner_name)]

repeat_champions <- title_counts[titles > 1L]
summary_b <- repeat_champions[, .(players = .N,
                                  highest_title_count = max(titles))]
leaders_b <- title_counts[titles == max(titles)]

print(summary_b)
print(leaders_b)
```

## c. Is there any evidence that winners have more aces than losers?

```{r}
ace_pairs <- ten[!is.na(w_ace) & !is.na(l_ace),
                 .(winner_ace = w_ace, loser_ace = l_ace)]

ace_summary <- ace_pairs[, .(
  matches = .N,
  average_winner = mean(winner_ace),
  average_loser = mean(loser_ace),
  average_difference = mean(winner_ace - loser_ace),
  median_difference = median(winner_ace - loser_ace),
  share_winner_more = mean(winner_ace > loser_ace),
  share_tied = mean(winner_ace == loser_ace)
)]
print(ace_summary)
```

winners perform more aces than losers.

## d. Identify the player(s) with the highest win-rate. Restrict to players with at least 5 matches.

```{r}
appearances <- rbindlist(list(
  ten[, .(player_id = winner_id,
          player_name = winner_name,
          won = 1L)],
  ten[, .(player_id = loser_id,
          player_name = loser_name,
          won = 0L)]
))

player_records <- appearances[!is.na(player_id), .(
  player_name = player_name[1L],
  matches = .N,
  victories = sum(won),
  win_rate = mean(won)
), by = player_id]

eligible_players <- player_records[matches >= 5L][
  order(-win_rate, -matches, player_name)
]

leaders_d <- eligible_players[win_rate == max(win_rate)]
print(eligible_players[seq_len(min(10L, nrow(eligible_players)))])
print(leaders_d)
```

So Rafael Nadal has the highest win-rate.

# Problem 3: poltly

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(plotly)

source_p3<- paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nytimes/covid-19-data/refs/heads/master/rolling-averages/us-states.csv")
covid_raw <- read.csv(source_p3, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
covid_raw$date <- as.Date(covid_raw$date)
state_data <- covid_raw %>%
  filter(state %in% state.name) %>%
  arrange(state, date)

stopifnot(nrow(state_data) > 0L)
```

## a. How many major and minor spikes in cases were there?

```{r}
national <- state_data %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarise(average_daily_cases = sum(cases_avg, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  mutate(trend = as.numeric(stats::filter(
    average_daily_cases, rep(1 / 21, 21), sides = 2
  )))

series <- national$trend
maximum <- max(series, na.rm = TRUE)

local_maximum <- vapply(seq_along(series), function(i) {
  if (!is.finite(series[i])) return(FALSE)
  j <- seq.int(max(1L, i - 30L), min(length(series), i + 30L))
  series[i] == max(series[j], na.rm = TRUE)
}, logical(1))

candidates <- which(local_maximum & series >= 0.04 * maximum)
by_height <- candidates[order(series[candidates], decreasing = TRUE)]

selected <- integer(0)
for (i in by_height) {
  if (length(selected) == 0L || all(abs(selected - i) >= 65L)) {
    selected <- c(selected, i)
  }
}

peaks <- national[sort(selected), ] %>%
  mutate(category = if_else(trend >= 0.15 * maximum, "Major", "Minor"))

peak_counts <- peaks %>% count(category, name = "number_of_peaks")
print(peaks %>% transmute(date, category,
                          cases_per_day = round(trend)))
print(peak_counts)

p_a <- plot_ly() %>%
  add_lines(
    data = national, x = ~date, y = ~trend,
    name = "21-day trend", line = list(color = "#34495E", width = 2),
    hovertemplate = "%{x|%b %d, %Y}<br>%{y:,.0f} cases/day<extra></extra>"
  ) %>%
  add_markers(
    data = filter(peaks, category == "Major"), x = ~date, y = ~trend,
    name = "Major peak", marker = list(color = "#C94B4B", size = 10),
    hovertemplate = "Major peak: %{x|%b %Y}<br>%{y:,.0f} cases/day<extra></extra>"
  ) %>%
  add_markers(
    data = filter(peaks, category == "Minor"), x = ~date, y = ~trend,
    name = "Minor peak", marker = list(color = "#E6A23C", size = 9),
    hovertemplate = "Minor peak: %{x|%b %Y}<br>%{y:,.0f} cases/day<extra></extra>"
  ) %>%
  layout(
    title = list(text = "COVID-19 case waves across the 50 U.S. states"),
    xaxis = list(title = "", tickformat = "%b %Y", showgrid = FALSE),
    yaxis = list(title = "Smoothed new cases per day", separatethousands = TRUE,
                 gridcolor = "#E6EAF0", zeroline = FALSE),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = -0.18),
    paper_bgcolor = "white", plot_bgcolor = "white",
    font = list(family = "Arial", color = "#233142")
  )
p_a
```

Under this peak-detection convention, I identify 4 major peaks and 4 minor peaks

## b. For the states with the highest and lowest overall rates per population, what differences do you see in their trajectories over time?

```{r}
ranked_states <- state_data %>%
  group_by(state) %>%
  summarise(approx_cases_per_100k = sum(cases_avg_per_100k, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(approx_cases_per_100k))

highest <- ranked_states$state[1]
lowest <- ranked_states$state[nrow(ranked_states)]

print(ranked_states %>% filter(state %in% c(highest, lowest)))

comparison <- state_data %>%
  filter(state %in% c(highest, lowest)) %>%
  mutate(state = factor(state, levels = c(highest, lowest)))

comparison_peaks <- comparison %>%
  group_by(state) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = cases_avg_per_100k, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(state, peak_date = date, peak_rate = cases_avg_per_100k)
print(comparison_peaks)

p_b <- plot_ly(
  comparison,
  x = ~date, y = ~cases_avg_per_100k, color = ~state,
  colors = c("#087E8B", "#C44536"),
  type = "scatter", mode = "lines", line = list(width = 2.5),
  hovertemplate = "%{fullData.name}<br>%{x|%b %d, %Y}<br>%{y:.1f} cases/100k<extra></extra>"
) %>%
  layout(
    title = list(text = "Reported COVID-19 incidence: highest vs. lowest overall"),
    xaxis = list(title = "", tickformat = "%b %Y", showgrid = FALSE),
    yaxis = list(title = "Seven-day average new cases per 100,000",
                 gridcolor = "#E6EAF0", zeroline = FALSE),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = -0.18),
    paper_bgcolor = "white", plot_bgcolor = "white",
    font = list(family = "Arial", color = "#233142")
  )
p_b
```

Rhode Island has the highest approximate cumulative reported rate , while Maine has the lowest.

## c. Identify, to the best of your ability without a formal test, the first five states to experience Covid in a substantial way.

```{r part-c}
first_wave <- state_data %>%
  filter(date <= as.Date("2020-06-30")) %>%
  group_by(state) %>%
  arrange(date, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    above_threshold = !is.na(cases_avg_per_100k) &
      cases_avg_per_100k >= 10,
    sustained = above_threshold &
      lead(above_threshold, 1, default = FALSE) &
      lead(above_threshold, 2, default = FALSE) &
      as.integer(lead(date, 1) - date) == 1L &
      as.integer(lead(date, 2) - date) == 2L
  ) %>%
  filter(sustained) %>%
  summarise(first_substantial_date = min(date), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(first_substantial_date, state) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5)

print(first_wave)
stopifnot(nrow(first_wave) == 5L)

state_order <- first_wave$state
start_date <- min(as.Date("2020-03-01"),
                  min(first_wave$first_substantial_date) - 10)
end_date <- max(as.Date("2020-05-15"),
                max(first_wave$first_substantial_date) + 21)

early_curves <- state_data %>%
  filter(state %in% state_order, date >= start_date, date <= end_date) %>%
  mutate(state = factor(state, levels = state_order))

crossings <- first_wave %>%
  left_join(
    select(state_data, state, date, cases_avg_per_100k),
    by = c("state" = "state", "first_substantial_date" = "date")
  ) %>%
  mutate(state = factor(state, levels = state_order))

palette <- c("#226D99", "#A23E48", "#F18F01", "#557C55", "#8055A2")

p_c <- plot_ly() %>%
  add_lines(
    data = early_curves,
    x = ~date, y = ~cases_avg_per_100k,
    color = ~state, colors = palette,
    line = list(width = 2.5),
    hovertemplate = "%{fullData.name}<br>%{x|%b %d, %Y}<br>%{y:.1f} cases/100k<extra></extra>"
  ) %>%
  add_markers(
    data = crossings,
    x = ~first_substantial_date, y = ~cases_avg_per_100k,
    color = ~state, colors = palette,
    showlegend = FALSE,
    marker = list(size = 10, line = list(color = "white", width = 1)),
    hovertemplate = "Threshold reached: %{x|%b %d, %Y}<br>%{y:.1f} cases/100k<extra></extra>"
  ) %>%
  layout(
    title = list(text = "Five earliest substantial state-level COVID-19 outbreaks"),
    xaxis = list(title = "", range = c(as.character(start_date), as.character(end_date)),
                 tickformat = "%b %d", showgrid = FALSE),
    yaxis = list(title = "Seven-day average new cases per 100,000",
                 gridcolor = "#E6EAF0", zeroline = FALSE),
    shapes = list(list(
      type = "line", xref = "paper", x0 = 0, x1 = 1,
      yref = "y", y0 = 10, y1 = 10,
      line = list(color = "#737D8C", width = 1.5, dash = "dot")
    )),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = -0.18),
    paper_bgcolor = "white", plot_bgcolor = "white",
    font = list(family = "Arial", color = "#233142")
  )
p_c
```

The first five states are New York, New Jersey, Massachusetts, Connecticut, Louisiana. Their first qualifying dates are New York — 2020-03-22; New Jersey — 2020-03-27; Massachusetts — 2020-03-30; Connecticut — 2020-03-31; Louisiana — 2020-03-31.
